claim: Autism spectrum disorder (ASD) is characterized by deficits in communication, diminished social skills, and stereotyped behaviors.
source: Autism spectrum disorder (ASD) is characterized by deficits in communication, diminished social skills, and stereotyped behaviors.
evidence: This is a definitional statement about ASD that draws from established scientific consensus.

claim: ASD is one of the most heritable of neuropsychiatric disorders.
source: It is one of the most heritable of neuropsychiatric disorders (Colvert et al., 2015).
evidence: Supported by citation to Colvert et al., 2015.

claim: Thousands of genetic variations, both common and rare, contribute to ASD risk.
source: Thousands of genetic variations, both common and rare, contribute to ASD risk (Geschwind and State, 2015).
evidence: Supported by citation to Geschwind and State, 2015.

claim: Chromatin remodeling is one of the top pathways disrupted in ASD.
source: Causative genes identified to date encode molecules involved in a myriad of molecular pathways, with chromatin remodeling being one of the top pathways disrupted in ASD (De Rubeis et al., 2014).
evidence: Supported by citation to De Rubeis et al., 2014.

claim: Identified genes account for only ~30% of ASD cases with no single gene contributing to greater than 2% of cases.
source: Despite recent strides being made in our understanding of the complex genetics of ASD, identified genes account for only ~30% of ASD cases with no single gene contributing to greater than 2% of cases (de la Torre-Ubieta et al., 2016; Dias and Walsh, 2020).
evidence: Supported by citations to de la Torre-Ubieta et al., 2016 and Dias and Walsh, 2020.

claim: The authors screened mice bearing N-ethyl-N-nitrosourea (ENU)-induced mutations for defects in ultrasonic vocalizations (USVs) and nest-building behavior.
source: We screened mice bearing N-ethyl-N-nitrosourea (ENU)-induced mutations (Wang et al., 2015) for defects in ultrasonic vocalizations (USVs) and nest-building behavior.
evidence: This describes the experimental approach used in the study.

claim: Automated meiotic mapping implicated Kdm5a as a candidate ASD gene.
source: Automated meiotic mapping implicated Kdm5a as a candidate ASD gene and a nonsense mutation at that locus segregated with defective USVs and nest building.
evidence: This describes the results of the mapping analysis performed in the study.

claim: A nonsense mutation in Kdm5a segregated with defective USVs and nest building.
source: Automated meiotic mapping implicated Kdm5a as a candidate ASD gene and a nonsense mutation at that locus segregated with defective USVs and nest building.
evidence: This describes the genetic finding from the study.

claim: Targeted knockout of Kdm5a resulted in repetitive behaviors, deficits in social interaction, learning, and memory, and abnormal neuronal morphology.
source: In addition to these phenotypes, targeted knockout of Kdm5a resulted in repetitive behaviors, deficits in social interaction, learning, and memory, and abnormal neuronal morphology.
evidence: This summarizes the behavioral and morphological phenotypes observed in the knockout mice.

claim: KDM5A encodes a chromatin regulator that belongs to the KDM5 family of lysine-specific histone H3 demethylases.
source: KDM5A encodes a chromatin regulator that belongs to the KDM5 family of lysine-specific histone H3 demethylases.
evidence: This is a statement about the molecular function of KDM5A based on established knowledge.

claim: Histone H3 lysine 4 trimethyl (H3K4me3) marks are present at gene promoters and active enhancers.
source: Histone H3 lysine 4 trimethyl (H3K4me3) marks are present at gene promoters and active enhancers, and are regulated by multiple factors, including the KDM5 family members KDM5B and KDM5C (Shen et al., 2017).
evidence: Supported by citation to Shen et al., 2017.

claim: H3K4me3 marks are regulated by multiple factors, including the KDM5 family members KDM5B and KDM5C.
source: Histone H3 lysine 4 trimethyl (H3K4me3) marks are present at gene promoters and active enhancers, and are regulated by multiple factors, including the KDM5 family members KDM5B and KDM5C (Shen et al., 2017).
evidence: Supported by citation to Shen et al., 2017.

claim: Mutations in lysine demethylases that regulate the demethylation of the H3K4me3 marks have been strongly linked to a host of neurodevelopmental disorders.
source: Mutations in lysine demethylases that regulate the demethylation of the H3K4me3 marks have been strongly linked to a host of neurodevelopmental disorders.
evidence: This is a general statement about the role of lysine demethylases in neurodevelopmental disorders based on established knowledge.

claim: The authors identified nine patients with ASD and lack of speech who have pathogenic KDM5A variants.
source: Finally, we identified nine patients with ASD and lack of speech who have pathogenic KDM5A variants.
evidence: This describes the clinical findings from the study.

claim: The authors screened ENU mutagenized mice for ASD-like behavioral phenotypes, specifically abnormalities in USVs and nest-building behavior.
source: To identify candidate ASD genes, we screened ENU mutagenized mice for ASD-like behavioral phenotypes. Specifically, we screened for abnormalities in USVs (Portfors, 2007) and in nest-building behavior (Crawley, 2004).
evidence: This describes the experimental approach with citations to support the use of these behavioral assays.

claim: USV quantification is a well-documented tool to assess social communication in mice.
source: USV quantification is a well-documented tool to assess social communication in mice (Scattoni et al., 2009; Branchi et al., 2001), and USV deficits are indicators of abnormal brain development.
evidence: Supported by citations to Scattoni et al., 2009 and Branchi et al., 2001.

claim: USV deficits are indicators of abnormal brain development.
source: USV quantification is a well-documented tool to assess social communication in mice (Scattoni et al., 2009; Branchi et al., 2001), and USV deficits are indicators of abnormal brain development.
evidence: This is a statement about the interpretation of USV deficits based on established knowledge and citations.

claim: Mouse models of neurodevelopmental disorders, including ASD models, tend to vocalize less frequently or display abnormal vocalization parameters compared to wild type mice.
source: Mouse models of neurodevelopmental disorders, including ASD models, tend to vocalize less frequently or display abnormal vocalization parameters compared to wild type (WT) mice (Lai et al., 2014).
evidence: Supported by citation to Lai et al., 2014.

claim: The ability to build a communal nest is an indicator of sociability in mice.
source: In addition, the ability to build a communal nest is an indicator of sociability in mice (Crawley, 2007).
evidence: Supported by citation to Crawley, 2007.

claim: The authors performed ENU mutagenesis in male C57BL/6J WT mice and bred them to obtain ~30–50 third generation (G3) mice per pedigree.
source: We performed ENU mutagenesis in male C57BL/6J WT mice as previously described (Wang et al., 2015) and bred them to obtain ~30–50 third generation (G3) mice per pedigree (Figure 1—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This describes the breeding scheme used in the study, with reference to a figure.

claim: All G1 males were subjected to whole exome sequencing.
source: All G1 males were subjected to whole exome sequencing, and all G2 and G3 mice from each pedigree were genotyped for variants identified in the G1 pedigree founder.
evidence: This describes the sequencing and genotyping approach used in the study.

claim: All G2 and G3 mice from each pedigree were genotyped for variants identified in the G1 pedigree founder.
source: All G1 males were subjected to whole exome sequencing, and all G2 and G3 mice from each pedigree were genotyped for variants identified in the G1 pedigree founder.
evidence: This describes the genotyping approach used in the study.

claim: The authors analyzed the ability of G3 mice to emit USVs at postnatal day (P) 4.
source: We analyzed the ability of G3 mice to emit USVs at postnatal day (P) 4, scoring several different USV parameters (Materials and methods), and measured the quality of nests built at P29-32.
evidence: This describes the timing of the USV analysis.

claim: The authors measured the quality of nests built at P29-32.
source: We analyzed the ability of G3 mice to emit USVs at postnatal day (P) 4, scoring several different USV parameters (Materials and methods), and measured the quality of nests built at P29-32.
evidence: This describes the timing of the nest-building analysis.

claim: For each USV parameter scored and for the nest-building behavior, mapping and linkage analysis was performed for every mutation, under the recessive, semidominant (additive), and dominant modes of inheritance, using Linkage Analyzer.
source: For each USV parameter scored and for the nest-building behavior, mapping and linkage analysis was performed for every mutation, under the recessive, semidominant (additive), and dominant modes of inheritance, using Linkage Analyzer which detects phenovariance statistically linked to genotype as determined by a linear regression model (Wang et al., 2015).
evidence: This describes the statistical analysis approach used in the study.

claim: Linkage Analyzer detects phenovariance statistically linked to genotype as determined by a linear regression model.
source: For each USV parameter scored and for the nest-building behavior, mapping and linkage analysis was performed for every mutation, under the recessive, semidominant (additive), and dominant modes of inheritance, using Linkage Analyzer which detects phenovariance statistically linked to genotype as determined by a linear regression model (Wang et al., 2015).
evidence: Supported by citation to Wang et al., 2015.

claim: The authors screened a total of 350 G3 mice in eight pedigrees, that carried 409 mutations.
source: We screened a total of 350 G3 mice in eight pedigrees, that carried 409 mutations, and identified a causative allelic variant (Selbst) with abnormal USVs and nesting behavior (Figure 1).
evidence: This describes the scale of the screen performed in the study.

claim: The authors identified a causative allelic variant (Selbst) with abnormal USVs and nesting behavior.
source: We screened a total of 350 G3 mice in eight pedigrees, that carried 409 mutations, and identified a causative allelic variant (Selbst) with abnormal USVs and nesting behavior (Figure 1).
evidence: This describes the main finding from the forward genetics screen.

claim: The Selbst phenotype showed clear recessive inheritance of reduced USV peak frequency.
source: The Selbst phenotype showed clear recessive inheritance of reduced USV peak frequency (Figure 1A and C) and impaired nest-building ability (Figure 1B and Figure 2—figure supplement 2B).
evidence: This describes the inheritance pattern and phenotype of the Selbst mutation, with reference to figures.

claim: The Selbst phenotype showed impaired nest-building ability.
source: The Selbst phenotype showed clear recessive inheritance of reduced USV peak frequency (Figure 1A and C) and impaired nest-building ability (Figure 1B and Figure 2—figure supplement 2B).
evidence: This describes the nest-building phenotype of the Selbst mutation, with reference to figures.

claim: Whole exome sequencing and mapping identified a single peak on chromosome 6 linked to both the USV (p=2.9×10−5) and the nesting (p=7.0×10−5) phenotypes.
source: Whole exome sequencing and mapping identified a single peak on chromosome 6 linked to both the USV (p=2.9×10−5) and the nesting (p=7.0×10−5) phenotypes (Figure 1D and E).
evidence: This describes the mapping results with statistical significance values.

claim: The peak on chromosome 6 corresponded to a single nucleotide substitution in Kdm5a resulting in a nonsense mutation (p.C322*).
source: The peak corresponded to a single nucleotide substitution in Kdm5a resulting in a nonsense mutation (p.C322*) predicted to cause loss of the protein.
evidence: This describes the specific mutation identified in Kdm5a.

claim: The Kdm5a p.C322* mutation is predicted to cause loss of the protein.
source: The peak corresponded to a single nucleotide substitution in Kdm5a resulting in a nonsense mutation (p.C322*) predicted to cause loss of the protein.
evidence: This is a prediction based on the nature of the nonsense mutation.

claim: Kdm5a encodes a chromatin regulator belonging to a family of histone lysine demethylases.
source: Kdm5a encodes a chromatin regulator belonging to a family of histone lysine demethylases.
evidence: This is a statement about the molecular function of Kdm5a based on established knowledge.

claim: Kdm5a is expressed ubiquitously in humans and mice.
source: It is expressed ubiquitously in humans and mice (Smith et al., 2019), including in the brain (Figure 1—figure supplement 2).
evidence: Supported by citation to Smith et al., 2019 and reference to a figure.

claim: Kdm5a is expressed in the brain.
source: It is expressed ubiquitously in humans and mice (Smith et al., 2019), including in the brain (Figure 1—figure supplement 2).
evidence: Supported by reference to a figure showing brain expression.

claim: The authors generated a Kdm5a constitutive knockout mouse model (Kdm5a-/-) using CRISPR/Cas9 technology.
source: In order to investigate the physiological function of KDM5A and to genetically confirm that the Kdm5a nonsense mutation is the cause of the Selbst phenotype, we generated a Kdm5a constitutive knockout mouse model (Kdm5a-/-). We targeted the mouse Kdm5a locus using CRISPR/Cas9 technology to insert a single base pair in exon 13, which was predicted to result in a frameshift mutation in codon 581 and to terminate translation after the inclusion of 8 aberrant amino acids (Figure 2A).
evidence: This describes the generation of the knockout mouse model.

claim: The Kdm5a knockout was predicted to result in a frameshift mutation in codon 581 and to terminate translation after the inclusion of 8 aberrant amino acids.
source: We targeted the mouse Kdm5a locus using CRISPR/Cas9 technology to insert a single base pair in exon 13, which was predicted to result in a frameshift mutation in codon 581 and to terminate translation after the inclusion of 8 aberrant amino acids (Figure 2A).
evidence: This is a prediction based on the nature of the frameshift mutation.

claim: Western blot analysis on cortical tissue demonstrated loss of KDM5A in Kdm5a-/- mice compared to WT and heterozygous littermates.
source: We performed western blot analysis on cortical tissue and demonstrated loss of KDM5A in Kdm5a-/- mice compared to WT and heterozygous littermates (Figure 2B).
evidence: This describes the western blot results confirming loss of protein in the knockout mice.

claim: Kdm5a-/- mice were born in expected Mendelian ratios.
source: Kdm5a-/- mice were born in expected Mendelian ratios, exhibited normal body weight, body length, and brain to body weight ratio compared with control littermates (WT and Kdm5a+/-) (Figure 2—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This describes the viability and basic physical characteristics of the knockout mice.

claim: Kdm5a-/- mice exhibited normal body weight, body length, and brain to body weight ratio compared with control littermates.
source: Kdm5a-/- mice were born in expected Mendelian ratios, exhibited normal body weight, body length, and brain to body weight ratio compared with control littermates (WT and Kdm5a+/-) (Figure 2—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This describes the basic physical characteristics of the knockout mice.

claim: Kdm5a-/- mice had reduced peak frequency of emitted USVs, which replicates the Selbst phenotype.
source: We found that Kdm5a-/- mice had reduced peak frequency of emitted USVs, which replicates the Selbst phenotype, and a severe reduction in the number of USVs (~84% decrease) compared with control littermates (Figure 2C and Figure 2—figure supplement 2A).
evidence: This describes the USV phenotype of the knockout mice, confirming the Selbst phenotype.

claim: Kdm5a-/- mice had a severe reduction in the number of USVs (~84% decrease) compared with control littermates.
source: We found that Kdm5a-/- mice had reduced peak frequency of emitted USVs, which replicates the Selbst phenotype, and a severe reduction in the number of USVs (~84% decrease) compared with control littermates (Figure 2C and Figure 2—figure supplement 2A).
evidence: This describes the USV phenotype of the knockout mice with a quantitative measure.

claim: Kdm5a-/- mice spent more time wringing and clasping their forepaws compared with control littermates.
source: We found that the Kdm5a-/- mice spent more time wringing and clasping their forepaws compared with control littermates (Figure 2D, Figure 2—video 1, and Figure 2—video 2).
evidence: This describes the forepaw wringing and clasping phenotype of the knockout mice.

claim: Kdm5a-/- mice spent twice as much time self-grooming compared to control littermates.
source: We also measured self-grooming behavior and found that Kdm5a-/- mice spent twice as much time self-grooming compared to control littermates (Figure 2E).
evidence: This describes the self-grooming phenotype of the knockout mice with a quantitative measure.

claim: Kdm5a-/- mice showed a slight increase in the total distance traveled in the open field test, indicating a mild hyperactivity phenotype.
source: We noticed a slight increase in the total distance traveled by the Kdm5a-/- mice, indicating a mild hyperactivity phenotype (Figure 2F).
evidence: This describes the locomotor activity phenotype of the knockout mice in the open field test.

claim: Kdm5a-/- mice spent significantly less time in the center of the open field arena indicating a possible anxiety phenotype.
source: In addition, we found that the Kdm5a-/- mice spent significantly less time in the center of the arena indicating a possible anxiety phenotype (Figure 2F).
evidence: This describes the anxiety-related behavior of the knockout mice in the open field test.

claim: Kdm5a-/- mice spent significantly less time (~50%) interacting with novel partner mice compared to control littermates.
source: To assess any social behavior deficits, we measured direct social interaction (Chang et al., 2017; Crawley, 2012) and found that the Kdm5a-/- mice spent significantly less time (~50%) interacting with novel partner mice compared to control littermates (Figure 2G).
evidence: This describes the social interaction phenotype of the knockout mice with a quantitative measure.

claim: Kdm5a-/- mice displayed severe disabilities in both learning and memory in the Morris water maze test.
source: However, Kdm5a-/- mice displayed severe disabilities in both learning and memory. Their latency to reach the hidden platform did not decrease over time and they did not show preference for the target quadrant during the probe test (Figure 2H and I).
evidence: This describes the learning and memory phenotype of the knockout mice in the Morris water maze test.

claim: The latency of Kdm5a-/- mice to reach the hidden platform in the Morris water maze did not decrease over time.
source: However, Kdm5a-/- mice displayed severe disabilities in both learning and memory. Their latency to reach the hidden platform did not decrease over time and they did not show preference for the target quadrant during the probe test (Figure 2H and I).
evidence: This describes the learning phenotype of the knockout mice in the Morris water maze test.

claim: Kdm5a-/- mice did not show preference for the target quadrant during the Morris water maze probe test.
source: However, Kdm5a-/- mice displayed severe disabilities in both learning and memory. Their latency to reach the hidden platform did not decrease over time and they did not show preference for the target quadrant during the probe test (Figure 2H and I).
evidence: This describes the memory phenotype of the knockout mice in the Morris water maze test.

claim: Sholl analysis revealed a severe reduction (~67%) in dendritic complexity of cortical neurons from Kdm5a-/- mice.
source: Sholl analysis revealed a severe reduction (~67%) in dendritic complexity of cortical neurons from Kdm5a-/- mice (Figure 3A and B).
evidence: This describes the dendritic complexity phenotype of neurons from knockout mice with a quantitative measure.

claim: Cortical neurons from Kdm5a-/- mice had significant reduction in dendritic length (∼50% decrease).
source: Furthermore, cortical neurons from Kdm5a-/- mice had significant reduction in dendritic length (∼50% decrease) and dendritic spine density (∼33% decrease) compared with neurons from WT littermates (Figure 3C and D).
evidence: This describes the dendritic length phenotype of neurons from knockout mice with a quantitative measure.

claim: Cortical neurons from Kdm5a-/- mice had significant reduction in dendritic spine density (∼33% decrease).
source: Furthermore, cortical neurons from Kdm5a-/- mice had significant reduction in dendritic length (∼50% decrease) and dendritic spine density (∼33% decrease) compared with neurons from WT littermates (Figure 3C and D).
evidence: This describes the dendritic spine density phenotype of neurons from knockout mice with a quantitative measure.

claim: The human homolog, KDM5A, is extremely intolerant to loss-of-function variation based on data from the Genome Aggregation Database (gnomAD) (probability of loss-of-function intolerance (pLI) = 1.00).
source: The human homolog, KDM5A, is extremely intolerant to loss-of-function variation based on data from the Genome Aggregation Database (gnomAD) (probability of loss-of-function intolerance (pLI) = 1.00) (Genome Aggregation Database Consortium et al., 2020).
evidence: This is a statement about the constraint of KDM5A based on gnomAD data.

claim: Prior to this study, it was not known whether KDM5A loss-of-function mutations result in ASD or in other neurodevelopmental disorders.
source: Prior to our study, it was not known whether KDM5A loss-of-function mutations result in ASD or in other neurodevelopmental disorders.
evidence: This is a statement about the state of knowledge prior to the study.

claim: A single recessive missense variant in KDM5A has been reported to be associated with an undefined developmental disorder (intellectual disability and facial dysmorphisms) in one family.
source: To date only a single recessive missense variant in KDM5A has been reported to be associated with an undefined developmental disorder (intellectual disability and facial dysmorphisms) in one family (Najmabadi et al., 2011).
evidence: Supported by citation to Najmabadi et al., 2011.

claim: Genes encoding other members of the KDM5 family, KDM5B and KDM5C, are disrupted in neurodevelopmental disorders.
source: It is worth noting that genes encoding other members of the KDM5 family, KDM5B and KDM5C, are disrupted in neurodevelopmental disorders (De Rubeis et al., 2014; Lebrun et al., 2018; Al-Mubarak et al., 2017; Adegbola et al., 2008; Vallianatos et al., 2018).
evidence: Supported by multiple citations.

claim: Through global collaborative efforts, the authors identified nine individuals from seven families where clinical whole exome sequencing or chromosomal microarray analysis revealed pathogenic variants in KDM5A that segregated with phenotype in these families.
source: Through global collaborative efforts, we identified nine individuals from seven families where clinical whole exome sequencing or chromosomal microarray analysis revealed pathogenic variants in KDM5A that segregated with phenotype in these families (Figure 4A and Clinical presentation).
evidence: This describes the identification of patients with KDM5A mutations.

claim: Apart from the KDM5A variants, no variants were identified in known disease-causing genes that accounted for the clinical phenotype of the nine individuals.
source: Apart from the KDM5A variants, no variants were identified in known disease-causing genes that accounted for the clinical phenotype of the nine individuals.
evidence: This describes the exclusion of other known disease-causing genes in the patients.

claim: Three individuals carried homozygous deletions removing four exons (in two individuals) or ten exons (in one individual) of KDM5A.
source: Three individuals carried homozygous deletions removing four exons (in two individuals) or ten exons (in one individual) of KDM5A, three individuals carried homozygous recessive variants (two splice site and one missense), and the remaining three individuals were heterozygous for de novo variants (two missense and one nonsense) (Figure 4B, Figure 4—figure supplement 1, Figure 4—figure supplement 2, and Table 1).
evidence: This describes the types of KDM5A mutations identified in the patients.

claim: Three individuals carried homozygous recessive variants (two splice site and one missense) in KDM5A.
source: Three individuals carried homozygous deletions removing four exons (in two individuals) or ten exons (in one individual) of KDM5A, three individuals carried homozygous recessive variants (two splice site and one missense), and the remaining three individuals were heterozygous for de novo variants (two missense and one nonsense) (Figure 4B, Figure 4—figure supplement 1, Figure 4—figure supplement 2, and Table 1).
evidence: This describes the types of KDM5A mutations identified in the patients.

claim: Three individuals were heterozygous for de novo variants (two missense and one nonsense) in KDM5A.
source: Three individuals carried homozygous deletions removing four exons (in two individuals) or ten exons (in one individual) of KDM5A, three individuals carried homozygous recessive variants (two splice site and one missense), and the remaining three individuals were heterozygous for de novo variants (two missense and one nonsense) (Figure 4B, Figure 4—figure supplement 1, Figure 4—figure supplement 2, and Table 1).
evidence: This describes the types of KDM5A mutations identified in the patients.

claim: All the identified KDM5A variants were absent from exome or genome sequencing data of 141,456 unrelated individuals in gnomAD, confirming their rarity.
source: All the identified variants were absent from exome or genome sequencing data of 141,456 unrelated individuals in gnomAD (Genome Aggregation Database Consortium et al., 2020), confirming their rarity.
evidence: This describes the rarity of the identified KDM5A variants based on gnomAD data.

claim: All nine individuals with KDM5A mutations presented clinically with ASD and a spectrum of neurodevelopmental phenotypes including complete lack of speech, intellectual disability, and developmental delay.
source: All nine individuals with KDM5A mutations presented clinically with ASD and a spectrum of neurodevelopmental phenotypes including complete lack of speech, intellectual disability, and developmental delay (Table 1 and Clinical presentation).
evidence: This describes the clinical phenotypes of the patients with KDM5A mutations.

claim: The proband from the first family (KD-1–3) was heterozygous for a missense mutation in the first methionine of KDM5A (p.Met1Leu).
source: The proband from the first family (KD-1–3) was heterozygous for a missense mutation in the first methionine of KDM5A (p.Met1Leu), which we validated via Sanger sequencing (Figure 4—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This describes the specific mutation in patient KD-1-3.

claim: The p.Met1Leu mutation alters the highly conserved initiation methionine in KDM5A.
source: The mutation alters the highly conserved initiation methionine in KDM5A (Figure 4—figure supplement 2A).
evidence: This describes the conservation of the residue affected by the mutation.

claim: Western blot analysis of lymphoblastoid cell lines showed a reduction in KDM5A in the proband KD-1-3 compared to the unaffected father.
source: Western blot analysis of lymphoblastoid cell lines showed a reduction in KDM5A in the proband compared to the unaffected father (Figure 4C).
evidence: This describes the impact of the mutation on KDM5A protein levels.

claim: Family KD-2 had two affected children homozygous for a ~ 10 kb deletion that removed exons 6 through 9 of KDM5A without disrupting the reading frame.
source: Family KD-2 had two affected children homozygous for a ~ 10 kb deletion that removed exons 6 through 9 of KDM5A without disrupting the reading frame (Figure 4—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This describes the specific deletion in patients KD-2-3 and KD-2-4.

claim: Western blot analysis of lymphoblastoid cell lines revealed a truncated protein of the predicted molecular weight (174 kDa) in the proband KD-2-4 compared to the unaffected parents.
source: Western blot analysis of lymphoblastoid cell lines revealed a truncated protein of the predicted molecular weight (174 kDa) in the proband compared to the unaffected parents (Figure 4C).
evidence: This describes the impact of the deletion on KDM5A protein.

claim: The proband in the third family (KD-3–3) was heterozygous for a missense mutation in a highly conserved arginine residue of KDM5A (p.Arg1428Leu).
source: The proband in the third family (KD-3–3) was heterozygous for a missense mutation in a highly conserved arginine residue of KDM5A (p.Arg1428Leu) (Figure 4—figure supplement 2B).
evidence: This describes the specific mutation in patient KD-3-3.

claim: The two affected children in family KD-4 carried a homozygous recessive variant disrupting the donor splice site of exon 18 (c.2541+1G > T).
source: The two affected children in family KD-4, who were offspring of a consanguineous mating, presented with the most severe phenotype that appeared to worsen with age given the phenotype of the older sibling (Table 1, Clinical presentation, Figure 4—video 1, and Figure 4—video 2). Both siblings carried a homozygous recessive variant disrupting the donor splice site of exon 18 (c.2541+1G > T).
evidence: This describes the specific mutation in patients KD-4-3 and KD-4-4.

claim: The splice site mutation c.2541+1G > T in KD-4 resulted in a severe reduction in KDM5A in the targeted cells compared to control cells.
source: We introduced this mutation into the KDM5A locus in HEK293T cells using CRISPR/Cas9 (Figure 4—figure supplement 1C) and analyzed its impact on KDM5A using western blot analysis. We found that the splice site mutation resulted in a severe reduction in KDM5A in the targeted cells compared to control cells (Figure 4C).
evidence: This describes the impact of the splice site mutation on KDM5A protein levels.

claim: Proband KD-5–3 was homozygous for a missense mutation in a highly conserved residue in KDM5A (p.Phe477Val).
source: Another proband, KD-5–3, was homozygous for a missense mutation in a highly conserved residue in KDM5A (p.Phe477Val, Figure 4—figure supplement 2C) and resulted in a reduction in KDM5A in lymphoblastoid cells from the proband compared to the unaffected family members (Figure 4C).
evidence: This describes the specific mutation in patient KD-5-3.

claim: The p.Phe477Val mutation resulted in a reduction in KDM5A in lymphoblastoid cells from the proband KD-5-3 compared to the unaffected family members.
source: Another proband, KD-5–3, was homozygous for a missense mutation in a highly conserved residue in KDM5A (p.Phe477Val, Figure 4—figure supplement 2C) and resulted in a reduction in KDM5A in lymphoblastoid cells from the proband compared to the unaffected family members (Figure 4C).
evidence: This describes the impact of the mutation on KDM5A protein levels.

claim: The proband in family KD-6 was heterozygous for a nonsense mutation in KDM5A that caused a reduction in KDM5A in the proband compared to the unaffected parents.
source: The proband in family KD-6 was heterozygous for a nonsense mutation in KDM5A that also caused a reduction in KDM5A in the proband compared to the unaffected parents (Figure 4C).
evidence: This describes the specific mutation in patient KD-6-3 and its impact on KDM5A protein levels.

claim: In family KD-7, the proband was homozygous for a ~ 50 kb deletion that removed exons 1 through 10 of KDM5A.
source: In family KD-7, the proband was homozygous for a ~ 50 kb deletion that removed exons 1 through 10 of KDM5A. The deletion is predicted to result in loss of KDM5A transcript and protein.
evidence: This describes the specific deletion in patient KD-7-3.

claim: The ~ 50 kb deletion in KD-7 is predicted to result in loss of KDM5A transcript and protein.
source: In family KD-7, the proband was homozygous for a ~ 50 kb deletion that removed exons 1 through 10 of KDM5A. The deletion is predicted to result in loss of KDM5A transcript and protein.
evidence: This is a prediction based on the nature of the deletion.

claim: KDM5A is a histone lysine demethylase that removes methyl groups from lysine 4 of histone H3, resulting in repression of target genes.
source: KDM5A is a histone lysine demethylase that removes methyl groups from lysine 4 of histone H3, resulting in repression of target genes.
evidence: This is a statement about the molecular function of KDM5A based on established knowledge.

claim: Loss of KDM5A resulted in dysregulation of 450 genes (FDR-corrected p≤0.05 and log2 fold change ≥|0.3|).
source: Loss of KDM5A resulted in dysregulation of 450 genes (FDR-corrected p≤0.05 and log2 fold change ≥|0.3|) (Figure 5—source data 1), of which 191 genes were upregulated and 259 genes were downregulated (Figure 5A and B).
evidence: This describes the RNA-seq results from the hippocampus of knockout mice.

claim: 191 genes were upregulated and 259 genes were downregulated in the hippocampus of Kdm5a-/- mice.
source: Loss of KDM5A resulted in dysregulation of 450 genes (FDR-corrected p≤0.05 and log2 fold change ≥|0.3|) (Figure 5—source data 1), of which 191 genes were upregulated and 259 genes were downregulated (Figure 5A and B).
evidence: This describes the RNA-seq results from the hippocampus of knockout mice.

claim: Upregulated genes in Kdm5a-/- hippocampus included those involved in the regulation of neurological processes (Ednrb, Gba, Mtmr2, Nov, Npy2r) and RNA splicing (Cdc40, Dhx38, Lsm3, Lsm8, Sart3, Sfswap, Snrpb2, Tfip11, Uhmk1, Wbp11).
source: Interestingly, upregulated genes included those involved in the regulation of neurological processes (Ednrb, Gba, Mtmr2, Nov, Npy2r) and RNA splicing (Cdc40, Dhx38, Lsm3, Lsm8, Sart3, Sfswap, Snrpb2, Tfip11, Uhmk1, Wbp11), while downregulated genes included those involved in neurogenesis (e.g. Myoc, Nphp1, Otx2, Sema3b, Sgk1, Six3os1, Trpv4) and cell proliferation (e.g. Ace, Adora2a, Aqp1, Cdh3, Enpp2, Nde1) (Figure 5—figure supplement 2B and Figure 5—figure supplement 2—source data 1).
evidence: This describes the functional categories of upregulated genes from the RNA-seq analysis.

claim: Downregulated genes in Kdm5a-/- hippocampus included those involved in neurogenesis (e.g. Myoc, Nphp1, Otx2, Sema3b, Sgk1, Six3os1, Trpv4) and cell proliferation (e.g. Ace, Adora2a, Aqp1, Cdh3, Enpp2, Nde1).
source: Interestingly, upregulated genes included those involved in the regulation of neurological processes (Ednrb, Gba, Mtmr2, Nov, Npy2r) and RNA splicing (Cdc40, Dhx38, Lsm3, Lsm8, Sart3, Sfswap, Snrpb2, Tfip11, Uhmk1, Wbp11), while downregulated genes included those involved in neurogenesis (e.g. Myoc, Nphp1, Otx2, Sema3b, Sgk1, Six3os1, Trpv4) and cell proliferation (e.g. Ace, Adora2a, Aqp1, Cdh3, Enpp2, Nde1) (Figure 5—figure supplement 2B and Figure 5—figure supplement 2—source data 1).
evidence: This describes the functional categories of downregulated genes from the RNA-seq analysis.

claim: Expression of the other members of the KDM5 family, Kdm5b, Kdm5c, and Kdm5d, remained unchanged upon loss of Kdm5a.
source: Expression of the other members of the KDM5 family, Kdm5b, Kdm5c, and Kdm5d, remained unchanged upon loss of Kdm5a (Figure 5—figure supplement 3).
evidence: This describes the expression of other KDM5 family members in the knockout mice.

claim: The most upregulated gene in Kdm5a-/- hippocampus was Efcab6 (log2 fold change = 1.34, FDR-corrected p=7.68×10−18).
source: The most upregulated gene, a potential direct target of KDM5A, was Efcab6 (EF-Hand Calcium Binding Domain 6; log2 fold change = 1.34, FDR-corrected p=7.68×10−18), which represses transcription of the androgen receptor by recruiting histone deacetylase complexes (Niki et al., 2003).
evidence: This describes the most upregulated gene from the RNA-seq analysis.

claim: Efcab6 represses transcription of the androgen receptor by recruiting histone deacetylase complexes.
source: The most upregulated gene, a potential direct target of KDM5A, was Efcab6 (EF-Hand Calcium Binding Domain 6; log2 fold change = 1.34, FDR-corrected p=7.68×10−18), which represses transcription of the androgen receptor by recruiting histone deacetylase complexes (Niki et al., 2003).
evidence: Supported by citation to Niki et al., 2003.

claim: The most downregulated gene in Kdm5a-/- hippocampus was Ptgds (log2 fold change = −1.13, FDR-corrected p=1.13×10−30).
source: The most downregulated gene was Ptgds (Prostaglandin D2 Synthase; log2 fold change = −1.13, FDR-corrected p=1.13×10−30), which functions as a neuromodulator and a trophic factor in the brain (Taniguchi et al., 2007).
evidence: This describes the most downregulated gene from the RNA-seq analysis.

claim: Ptgds functions as a neuromodulator and a trophic factor in the brain.
source: The most downregulated gene was Ptgds (Prostaglandin D2 Synthase; log2 fold change = −1.13, FDR-corrected p=1.13×10−30), which functions as a neuromodulator and a trophic factor in the brain (Taniguchi et al., 2007).
evidence: Supported by citation to Taniguchi et al., 2007.

claim: Out of 450 differentially expressed genes in Kdm5a-/- hippocampus, 15 were homologs of known ASD genes.
source: Out of 450 differentially expressed genes, 15 were homologs of known ASD genes, including Ace, Cnr1, Mfrp, Oxtr, and Ppp1r1b, and 33 were homologs of genes essential for brain development, including Cdh3, Otx2, Pcolce2, and Sema3b, highlighting the importance of KDM5A in brain development and function.
evidence: This describes the overlap of dysregulated genes with known ASD genes.

claim: Out of 450 differentially expressed genes in Kdm5a-/- hippocampus, 33 were homologs of genes essential for brain development.
source: Out of 450 differentially expressed genes, 15 were homologs of known ASD genes, including Ace, Cnr1, Mfrp, Oxtr, and Ppp1r1b, and 33 were homologs of genes essential for brain development, including Cdh3, Otx2, Pcolce2, and Sema3b, highlighting the importance of KDM5A in brain development and function.
evidence: This describes the overlap of dysregulated genes with genes essential for brain development.

claim: This is the first successful identification of an ASD gene through a forward genetics strategy.
source: By screening ENU mutagenized mice for ASD-like behaviors, we identified Kdm5a as a candidate ASD gene that regulates vocalization and nesting. To our knowledge, this is the first successful identification of an ASD gene through a forward genetics strategy.
evidence: This is a claim about the novelty of the approach used in the study.

claim: In the screen, damaging homozygous mutations were observed in ~0.2% of all genes in three or more mice.
source: In our screen, we observed damaging homozygous mutations in ~0.2% of all genes in three or more mice, and we were able to successfully identify a candidate ASD gene, indicating the efficiency of this strategy for highly heterogeneous disorders.
evidence: This describes the frequency of damaging mutations observed in the screen.

claim: The forward genetics strategy is efficient for highly heterogeneous disorders.
source: In our screen, we observed damaging homozygous mutations in ~0.2% of all genes in three or more mice, and we were able to successfully identify a candidate ASD gene, indicating the efficiency of this strategy for highly heterogeneous disorders.
evidence: This is an inference based on the success of the screen.

claim: Forepaw wringing and clasping is a characteristic ASD-like phenotype observed in mouse models of several neurodevelopmental disorders, one of the most well-characterized examples being mouse models of Rett syndrome.
source: Furthermore, Kdm5a-/- mice showed increased self-grooming and remarkable repetitive forepaw wringing and clasping, a characteristic ASD-like phenotype observed in mouse models of several neurodevelopmental disorders, one of the most well-characterized examples being mouse models of Rett syndrome (Chao et al., 2010).
evidence: Supported by citation to Chao et al., 2010.

claim: Loss of KDM5A resulted in severe neuronal morphogenesis abnormalities, which included a decrease in dendritic complexity, length, and spine density.
source: In addition, loss of KDM5A resulted in severe neuronal morphogenesis abnormalities, which included a decrease in dendritic complexity, length, and spine density. These findings reveal an essential role for KDM5A in dendritic morphogenesis and maturation, processes essential for the establishment of neuronal circuitry and wiring of the brain (Dong et al., 2015).
evidence: This summarizes the neuronal morphology findings from the study.

claim: Dendritic morphogenesis and maturation are processes essential for the establishment of neuronal circuitry and wiring of the brain.
source: In addition, loss of KDM5A resulted in severe neuronal morphogenesis abnormalities, which included a decrease in dendritic complexity, length, and spine density. These findings reveal an essential role for KDM5A in dendritic morphogenesis and maturation, processes essential for the establishment of neuronal circuitry and wiring of the brain (Dong et al., 2015).
evidence: Supported by citation to Dong et al., 2015.

claim: The neurobehavioral phenotypes observed in the Kdm5a-/- mice recapitulate phenotypes observed in patients with KDM5A mutations, including deficits in sociability, cognitive function, and repetitive behaviors.
source: Collectively, the neurobehavioral phenotypes observed in the Kdm5a-/- mice uncover the function of KDM5A in the brain and recapitulate phenotypes observed in patients with KDM5A mutations, including deficits in sociability, cognitive function, and repetitive behaviors.
evidence: This is a summary statement comparing the mouse and human phenotypes.

claim: Chromatin regulation is essential for gene expression and brain development.
source: Chromatin regulation is essential for gene expression and brain development.
evidence: This is a general statement about the importance of chromatin regulation based on established knowledge.

claim: Mutations in several genes coding for chromatin remodelers and epigenetic modulators have been linked to neurodevelopmental disorders including ASD.
source: Mutations in several genes coding for chromatin remodelers and epigenetic modulators have been linked to neurodevelopmental disorders including ASD, with causative mutations identified in several chromatin remodelers (e.g. CHD8 and ARID1B) (O'Roak et al., 2012; Turner et al., 2016).
evidence: Supported by citations to O'Roak et al., 2012 and Turner et al., 2016.

claim: Two genes in the KDM5 family, KDM5B and KDM5C, are disrupted in neurodevelopmental disorders, including intellectual disability and ASD.
source: Moreover, two genes in the KDM5 family, KDM5B and KDM5C, are disrupted in neurodevelopmental disorders, including intellectual disability and ASD (De Rubeis et al., 2014; Iossifov et al., 2014; Jensen et al., 2005).
evidence: Supported by multiple citations.

claim: This is the first report implicating disruption of KDM5A as a cause of ASD.
source: This is the first report implicating disruption of KDM5A as a cause of ASD.
evidence: This is a claim about the novelty of the findings.

claim: The fact that mutations in KDM5A, KDM5B, and KDM5C all cause neurodevelopmental disorders, indicates that their function in the brain is nonredundant.
source: The fact that mutations in KDM5A, KDM5B, and KDM5C all cause neurodevelopmental disorders, indicates that their function in the brain is nonredundant.
evidence: This is an inference based on the observation that mutations in all three genes cause neurodevelopmental disorders.

claim: All the patients with KDM5A mutations reported in this study have a complete absence of speech, suggesting a potential role for KDM5A in regulating social communication in humans.
source: Despite the phenotypic variability typically observed within the different genetic subtypes of ASD, all the patients with KDM5A mutations reported in our study have a complete absence of speech, suggesting a potential role for KDM5A in regulating social communication in humans.
evidence: This is an inference based on the consistent phenotype of absent speech in all patients.

claim: Both inherited and de novo mutations were identified in KDM5A, similar to many other ASD genes including KDM5B, CHD8, and DOCK8.
source: Both inherited and de novo mutations were identified in KDM5A, similar to many other ASD genes including KDM5B (Lebrun et al., 2018), CHD8 (Guo et al., 2018), and DOCK8 (De Rubeis et al., 2014; Guo et al., 2018).
evidence: Supported by multiple citations.

claim: The recessive missense mutation in KD-5 results in a single amino acid substitution in one of the enzymatic domains of KDM5A, the Jumanji C (JmjC) domain.
source: The recessive missense mutation in KD-5 results in a single amino acid substitution in one of the enzymatic domains of KDM5A, the Jumanji C (JmjC) domain (Pilka et al., 2015; Horton et al., 2016).
evidence: Supported by citations to Pilka et al., 2015 and Horton et al., 2016.

claim: The homozygous deletion in KD-2 results in loss of the plant homeodomain 1 (PHD1), which binds unmodified H3K4.
source: The homozygous deletion in KD-2 results in loss of the plant homeodomain 1 (PHD1), which binds unmodified H3K4 (Torres et al., 2015) and was shown to enhance the demethylase catalytic activity (Longbotham et al., 2019).
evidence: Supported by citations to Torres et al., 2015 and Longbotham et al., 2019.

claim: PHD1 was shown to enhance the demethylase catalytic activity of KDM5A.
source: The homozygous deletion in KD-2 results in loss of the plant homeodomain 1 (PHD1), which binds unmodified H3K4 (Torres et al., 2015) and was shown to enhance the demethylase catalytic activity (Longbotham et al., 2019).
evidence: Supported by citation to Longbotham et al., 2019.

claim: The fact that the KD-2 deletion results in a truncated protein which is also present in the healthy carrier parents argues against the mutation being dominant negative.
source: Furthermore, the fact that the KD-2 deletion results in a truncated protein which is also present in the healthy carrier parents argues against the mutation being dominant negative.
evidence: This is an inference based on the observation that the truncated protein is present in healthy carriers.

claim: The fact that both monoallelic as well as biallelic mutations in KDM5A were identified emphasizes the sensitivity of the brain to KDM5A levels.
source: The fact that we identified both monoallelic as well as biallelic mutations in KDM5A emphasizes the sensitivity of the brain to KDM5A levels.
evidence: This is an inference based on the observation of both monoallelic and biallelic mutations.

claim: KDM5A demethylates H3K4me3, a histone mark known to be associated with memory formation.
source: KDM5A demethylates H3K4me3, a histone mark known to be associated with memory formation (Collins et al., 2019a; Gupta et al., 2010) and memory retrieval (Webb et al., 2017).
evidence: Supported by citations to Collins et al., 2019a, Gupta et al., 2010, and Webb et al., 2017.

claim: H3K4me3 is a histone mark known to be associated with memory retrieval.
source: KDM5A demethylates H3K4me3, a histone mark known to be associated with memory formation (Collins et al., 2019a; Gupta et al., 2010) and memory retrieval (Webb et al., 2017).
evidence: Supported by citation to Webb et al., 2017.

claim: Perturbations in histone demethylases and methyltransferases at the H3K4me3 mark give rise to neurodevelopmental disorders, including ASD and intellectual disability.
source: Perturbations in histone demethylases and methyltransferases at this mark give rise to neurodevelopmental disorders, including ASD and intellectual disability (Vallianatos and Iwase, 2015), emphasizing the importance of H3K4me3 in learning and memory (Collins et al., 2019b).
evidence: Supported by citations to Vallianatos and Iwase, 2015 and Collins et al., 2019b.

claim: H3K4me3 is important in learning and memory.
source: Perturbations in histone demethylases and methyltransferases at this mark give rise to neurodevelopmental disorders, including ASD and intellectual disability (Vallianatos and Iwase, 2015), emphasizing the importance of H3K4me3 in learning and memory (Collins et al., 2019b).
evidence: Supported by citation to Collins et al., 2019b.

claim: By demethylating H3K4me3, an activating histone mark, KDM5A would be expected to repress the expression of its target genes.
source: By demethylating H3K4me3, an activating histone mark, KDM5A would be expected to repress the expression of its target genes, suggesting that genes upregulated in the hippocampus of the Kdm5a-/- mice are potential direct targets of KDM5A.
evidence: This is an inference based on the known function of KDM5A as a demethylase.

claim: Genes upregulated in the hippocampus of the Kdm5a-/- mice are potential direct targets of KDM5A.
source: By demethylating H3K4me3, an activating histone mark, KDM5A would be expected to repress the expression of its target genes, suggesting that genes upregulated in the hippocampus of the Kdm5a-/- mice are potential direct targets of KDM5A.
evidence: This is an inference based on the known function of KDM5A as a demethylase.

claim: Genes upregulated in Kdm5a-/- hippocampus clustered in regulation of neurological processes and RNA splicing, suggesting a role for KDM5A in these pathways.
source: Genes upregulated in Kdm5a-/- clustered in regulation of neurological processes and RNA splicing, suggesting a role for KDM5A in these pathways.
evidence: This is an inference based on the GO analysis of upregulated genes.

claim: Shh plays an essential role in hippocampal neurogenesis and neural progenitor cell proliferation and differentiation.
source: In addition, Shh, which plays an essential role in hippocampal neurogenesis and neural progenitor cell proliferation and differentiation, and its downstream target Ccnd1, were also upregulated in Kdm5a-/-, indicating a potential mechanism by which KDM5A could be exerting its function in the hippocampus.
evidence: This is a statement about the function of Shh based on established knowledge.

claim: Shh and its downstream target Ccnd1 were upregulated in Kdm5a-/- hippocampus, indicating a potential mechanism by which KDM5A could be exerting its function in the hippocampus.
source: In addition, Shh, which plays an essential role in hippocampal neurogenesis and neural progenitor cell proliferation and differentiation, and its downstream target Ccnd1, were also upregulated in Kdm5a-/-, indicating a potential mechanism by which KDM5A could be exerting its function in the hippocampus.
evidence: This is an inference based on the upregulation of Shh and Ccnd1 in the knockout mice.

claim: Downregulated genes in Kdm5a-/- hippocampus were involved in neurogenesis and cell proliferation, suggesting that loss of KDM5A altered these processes that are essential for normal hippocampal function.
source: Downregulated genes were involved in neurogenesis and cell proliferation, suggesting that loss of KDM5A altered these processes that are essential for normal hippocampal function.
evidence: This is an inference based on the GO analysis of downregulated genes.

claim: The transcriptomics data identify many neuronal genes perturbed in the hippocampus of Kdm5a-/- mice, and point to potential pathways through which KDM5A mediates its function in the brain.
source: Taken together, our transcriptomics data identify many neuronal genes perturbed in the hippocampus of Kdm5a-/- mice, and point to potential pathways through which KDM5A mediates its function in the brain.
evidence: This is a summary statement about the transcriptomics findings.

claim: The approach of leveraging forward genetics in mice underscores the value of this method to discover new gene defects that cause phenotypically complex and genetically heterogeneous disorders.
source: Our approach underscores the value of leveraging forward genetics in mice to discover new gene defects that cause phenotypically complex and genetically heterogeneous disorders.
evidence: This is a summary statement about the value of the forward genetics approach.
